title: Seeking God
lead: "Seek the LORD" is one of the Bible's basic descriptions of a life turned toward God: asking for his guidance, worshiping him, obeying him and depending on him. The promise attached to it, that those who seek him with all their heart will find him, runs from Moses through the prophets to Jesus.

sections.b: Moses promised Israel in exile, "you will find him, when you seek him with all your heart and with all your being" (Deuteronomy 4:29). Prophets repeat the call (Isaiah 55:6; Jeremiah 29:13; Amos 5:4–6; Hosea 10:12), and the psalms speak of seeking God's face (Psalm 27:8; Psalm 105:4). Chronicles makes the verb darash the measure of every king (1 Chronicles 10:13–14; 2 Chronicles 7:14; 2 Chronicles 15:2). Jesus says, "Keep looking, and you will find" (Matthew 7:7), and Hebrews that God rewards those who seek him (Hebrews 11:6).
